body:
Founder real-time: 'set up a bot queue... replace TDMB call it QUEUE... 3 bots - 4 player games... network queue... architect the bots the same way the bots work for brawlpit... packet level bots just like brawlpit.' Real, new MODE_QUEUE (protocol.h + Go mirror), server-side queue_activate_match() -- deliberately no in-process bot puppet logic at all, since QUEUE's population is filled entirely by real, separate emily-bot processes (given a new -mode flag) connecting via real UDP exactly like a human client, matching BRAWLPIT's real rl_bot_pool.py precedent more literally than BRAWLPIT's own ordinary matchmaker bot-fill (which is actually the same in-process-puppet pattern SHANKPIT's existing MODE_TDMO already used). Client: LOBBY_TDMB replaced by LOBBY_QUEUE (label 'QUEUE'), now a real networked connect instead of the old fully-local bot battle. New ops/shankpit-bot-pool.sh + systemd unit run 3 standing real bot processes (NOT enabled against live prod by this commit -- left for an explicit go-ahead since it's a real, visible action on shared state). Two real bugs found and fixed live while verifying under NET_VERBOSE_LOG=1: a pre-existing undeclared 'mode_before' variable (invisible under the default build since the log macro strips it), and a real scene_id desync where the first connecting QUEUE player landed on a different scene than the next two. Live-verified end to end on an isolated test port (not the live :6969 production server) -- 3 real bot processes connected, correct scene sync, sustained real gameplay traffic. All build paths clean (Makefile, Bazel, go build, Windows cross-compile). Real CI green on both workflows, release v0.26.0 cut clean. Commits SHANKPIT fa93916 + 56c9ecc (changelog).

⚓ ☃
title: Real networked bot queue shipped -- MODE_QUEUE, packet-level bots (S459-34)
